body: Quick pass (M5) @ d36f2381: merges cleanly with main. The author's gate is green: tool_library 13, tool_library_holders 5, view_prefs 7, holder_library 11, tool_body* 40, project_roundtrip 71, mcp 13, ui lib 533, clippy clean, no snapshot PNGs. The body is complete (Changelog, Fixes #889, fork tag). It includes a process-file edit (camcraft-mcp skill) with a PROCESS_VERSION bump to 17, which collides with other open process PRs; whichever merges later renumbers. #889 is P2. Flagged ready for an independent review. It's a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut.

M3 note on top of the clean review: the "no stale verdict" argument relies on import being add-only. PR #1060 (merge-ready, a feat) adds Update-in-place and Replace import modes. Once both land, an Update with "Import tool holders" on rewrites an existing tool's body, so it must stale that tool's ops the way `ChangeTool` does (#1060 already stales on a geometry update; check it covers a body change). Whichever of #1060 and #1100 merges second should pin that case.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d36f23819158458e61e03692cb5f3ece714c49df -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`, so it merges at the next cut). No blockers found. Below is what I built, ran and tried.

Head `d36f2381` already contains current `origin/main`, so the trial merge was a no-op. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is bumped 16 -> 17 for the camcraft-mcp skill line, as the process law requires.

### What looks good
- **One read path.** The GUI page (`state_tool_library.rs`), MCP `import_tool_library` and the script verb all go `parse_tool_library` -> `read_body` -> `ImportTools::with_holders`. `read_body` uses the same `ToolBodyDto::to_body` + `tool_body::fits` that `project::validate` uses, and the command checks `fits` again. I found no path that skips it. This branch has no `Update`/`Replace` modes and no drag-and-drop import.
- **No file reads from the body.** A placed-mesh body embeds its facets; `source` is a label only and is never opened. So there is no path-traversal or absolute-path surface.
- **Whole file or nothing.** Every body is judged during parsing, before the command exists. A refusal names the tool and leaves no tool and no history entry (pinned by `a_malformed_or_ill_fitting_body_refuses_the_file_by_name`).
- **Holders off.** Tools land with the holder cylinder from their own record. The status line and the MCP reply say "N holders in the file not imported" (`holders_left_out`), so the loss is named rather than silent. The skip identity is sound: a bare-landing tool matches on the record only, and a tool landing with a body must match the body too, otherwise it arrives as "Name (2)" and never overwrites the document's holder.
- **Format.** Stays `camcraft-tools/1`. Main's `tool_from_json` has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so an older build drops `body`. Export writes bodies, and export -> import -> export is byte-stable (pinned).
- **Prefs.** The toggle lives in the per-user prefs file (`importToolHolders`, written only when false), not in the project or the history.

### Local results (Windows, debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app `tool_library` | 13 passed |
| app `tool_library_holders` | 5 passed |
| app `view_prefs` | 7 passed |
| app `mcp` | 13 passed |
| ui `--lib tool_library` / `--lib structural` (CWD crates/ui) | 3 / 4 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Hostile-file probe.** This was a local test, not pushed, built on the suite's own `source()` fixture, with holders on:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Negative spun radius | refused by name |
| `r = 1e300` | refused by name |
| `z = 1e300` | refused ("larger than any tool a spindle carries") |
| Empty facets | refused by name |
| Zero-area facets | refused by name |
| Facets at 1e12 | refused by name |
| Facets reaching into the flutes | refused ("does not surround the tool axis") |
| A lathe placement on a milling tool | refused by name |
| 200,000 facets | refused in ~1 s, no hang |

None of these panicked.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Placement metadata is not checked on load.** A placed-mesh body with `"offset": -1e9`, `"offset": 1e300` or `"axis": [0,0,0]` is **accepted**, and the garbage is stored. The derived envelope comes from the facets, so the collision input itself is sound. This is the project loader's behaviour too (`tool_body::build` does not re-check the axis/offset that `tool_body::place` refuses), so it is not new here. Still, a file can now carry it into a document; a follow-up issue to check axis/offset in `build` (as `place` does) seems worthwhile.
- **Holders off still checks bodies.** A file whose body is bad is refused even when the bodies would be thrown away. That is conservative and fine; it may just surprise someone.
- `cam.importTools(path)` is fixed to holders on. That is documented in the decision file, and MCP has the flag.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs` (1933 lines) grows by 9 lines. It was already far over 400, so this is noted, not blocking.
- **Not exercised:** the GUI by hand (the checkbox and the persistence across restarts beyond `view_prefs`), and the release lanes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
